newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica 1996 net seen up 20.2 percent.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica 1996 net seen up 20.2 percent.

text.p: Spanish telecommunications group Telefonica de Espana's earnings are expected to have risen 20.2 percent last year, given growth at home and abroad and a less troublesome debt burden, analysts said.

Telefonica, currently in the middle of the sale of the state's remaining 20.9 percent stake, will release highlights from its annual earnings after market close on Wednesday. Complete results will be published on February 28.
Net attributable profits are seen having risen by 20.2 percent to 159.9 million pesetas, as the company announced earlier, analysts said.

Operating income is seen having risen 13 percent to 1.96 billion pesetas while operating margin, which subtracts from costs and amortisation from operating income, is expected to have climbed 7.6 percent to 1.09 billion.
"The results of Telefonica will not offer any great surprise. The company itself said the objective was earning 160 billion pesetas in 1996," an analyst at a Spanish brokerage said.
The profit growth stems from growth both domestically and abroad as well as from a slowing in the rise in operating costs and a steady improvement in the group's finances.

Given debt of some two trillion pesetas, the drop in Spanish interest rates last year relieved pressure on the group. Spain's leading money market rate fell 2.75 percentage points in 1996 and long-term yields also declined sharply.
One of the company's few recent reversals was the steep expenditure made to promote mobile telephones, that apparently did not bring the benefits expected.
"With reference to earnings, it seems that the mobile telephone business contributed less in the final quarter than had been originally expected," an analyst at a independent research institute said.
As a result, Telefonica has already changed its marketing strategy and will no longer be giving away the mobile phone sets, local media said.
Apart from that small faux pas, experts agreed that Telefonica's future continued to be promising.
Its current monopoly in basic telephone services will only slowly be undermined by the arrival of new operator Retevision, while foreign holdings will contribute ever more to earnings.
The independent analyst said he expected group net profit to continue to grow 16.5 percent annually in the next few years.
Telefonica's sale is also going well. According to press reports, the offering is many times oversubscribed.
